blocks.text: 1. Large-Scale Enterprise RAG
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214176-610317116.png

Multi-Agent RAG System closed by pointing toward a simple, single-purpose task as a better fit for a lighter design. Large-Scale Enterprise RAG, a design combining every technique in this course to serve millions of queries across a massive knowledge base, closes the RAG System Design module and this entire course by bringing everything together at once.
It integrates retrieval, generation, evaluation, and production concerns into one complete, real-world system.
2. The Design Problem's Scope
This design combines the largest corpus, the widest user base, and the highest reliability bar covered anywhere in this course.
No single earlier system design alone covers every requirement this scale actually demands.

blocks.text: 3. Hybrid Retrieval Combining Vector And Graph Approaches

blocks.alt: Hybrid Retrieval Combining Vector And Graph Approaches
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214178-36989940.png
As with neither method covers everything in Hybrid Retrieval, vector search alone misses precise relationship chains that graph traversal finds.
Combining both retrieval methods covers the widest possible range of enterprise query types.
4. Multi-Tenant Isolation At Organization Scale
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214178-539392724.png
A large enterprise deployment often serves many separate business units or client organizations at once.
The same hard tenant isolation boundary applies at this larger scale too.
5. Full Observability Across Every Pipeline Stage

blocks.alt: Full Observability Across Every Pipeline Stage
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214179-58422512.png
As with observability combining metrics, logs, and traces in Observability, at this scale, a silent failure in any single stage can affect thousands of users before anyone notices.
Full metrics, logs, and tracing become mandatory, not optional, at enterprise scale.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A stage-level failure affecting even a small percentage of requests, translates into thousands of affected users at true enterprise query volume, exactly why full observability stops being optional at this scale.

6. Continuous Evaluation As A Standing Process

blocks.alt: Continuous Evaluation As A Standing Process
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214180-583166011.png
As with human evaluation validates automated metrics in Human Evaluation, a system this large needs ongoing evaluation, not a one-time quality check at launch.
Automated metrics run continuously, with periodic human evaluation sampling to keep them honest.

blocks.text: 7. Horizontal Scaling Across Every Layer Independently

blocks.alt: Horizontal Scaling Across Every Layer Independently
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214180-669912242.png

As with the vector database often scales differently than the rest in Scaling Strategies, application servers, the vector index, and the embedding pipeline each need their own independent scaling plan.
A single shared scaling strategy cannot serve every layer's different bottleneck.
8. Cost Discipline At This Size Directly Affects The Budget
As with caching remains the biggest single lever for cost in Cost Optimization, at millions of queries, even a small per-query cost multiplies into a very large total bill.
Aggressive caching and model right-sizing become a real financial necessity, not a nice-to-have.
9. Recognizing When This Specific Large-Scale Enterprise RAG Design Fits The Actual Need

blocks.alt: Recognizing When This Specific Large-Scale Enterprise RAG Design Fits The Actual Need
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785448214181-854554998.png
An organization operating at true enterprise scale with millions of queries fits this design.
A smaller, focused system is better served by one of the narrower designs earlier in this module.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates tenant-scoped hybrid retrieval combined with per-layer scaling awareness and cost tracking.

code.content:
import time

vector_chunks = [{"id": "v1", "tenant": "org_a", "text": "Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month."}]
graph_facts = [{"id": "g1", "tenant": "org_a", "fact": "Falcon Cloud supplies Acme Corp."}]

STAGE_COST = {"vector_search": 0.0002, "graph_traversal": 0.0003, "generation": 0.01}

def tenant_scoped_hybrid_retrieve(query, tenant_id):
    # hybrid retrieval combining vector and graph approaches
    v_results = [c for c in vector_chunks if c["tenant"] == tenant_id]
    g_results = [f for f in graph_facts if f["tenant"] == tenant_id]
    return v_results, g_results

def estimate_query_cost(v_results, g_results):
    # cost discipline at this size directly affects the budget
    cost = STAGE_COST["generation"]
    if v_results:
        cost += STAGE_COST["vector_search"]
    if g_results:
        cost += STAGE_COST["graph_traversal"]
    return cost

def log_request(tenant_id, query, cost):
    # full observability across every pipeline stage
    return {"tenant": tenant_id, "query": query, "cost": cost, "timestamp": time.time()}

query = "What does the Falcon plan cost and who does it supply?"
v_results, g_results = tenant_scoped_hybrid_retrieve(query, "org_a")
cost = estimate_query_cost(v_results, g_results)
log_entry = log_request("org_a", query, cost)

print("Large-scale enterprise RAG example:")
print(f"Vector results: {v_results}")
print(f"Graph results: {g_results}")
print(f"Estimated cost: ${cost:.5f}")
print(f"Log entry: {log_entry}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows tenant-scoped retrieval combining both vector and graph results while tracking per-query cost and logging the request, exactly the integrated hybrid retrieval, tenant isolation, cost, and observability.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Relying on only vector or only graph retrieval instead of combining both at enterprise scale.
Treating one shared scaling plan as sufficient for the app layer, vector index, and embedding pipeline.
Running quality evaluation only once at launch instead of as a continuous, ongoing process.
Underestimating how a small per-query cost multiplies into a very large bill at millions of queries.

blocks.text: 12. RAG & Vector Search: Course Complete

items: Large-scale enterprise RAG combines hybrid retrieval, multi-tenancy, observability, evaluation, scaling, and cost discipline into one system.
No single narrower design alone covers every requirement true enterprise scale demands.
Combining vector and graph retrieval covers the widest possible range of enterprise query types.
Hard tenant isolation, applies at this larger scale exactly as it does at smaller scale.
Full observability becomes mandatory once a silent failure can affect thousands of users at once.
Continuous evaluation, not a one-time launch check is required to catch quality drift over time.
Every layer, from app servers to the vector index to the embedding pipeline needs its own scaling plan.
Aggressive cost discipline becomes a financial necessity once per-query costs multiply at true scale.
This closes the RAG System Design module and the entire RAG & Vector Search course.
